body: The cleanup effect captures `backdropRef.current` into `backdropElement` at effect setup time. If the backdrop ref is null on the first run (or later points at a different element), the cleanup may fail to remove the `data-swiping` attribute, leaving the backdrop in a swiping state for the remainder of its lifetime. Read `backdropRef.current` inside the cleanup instead so the latest element is used.

🟡 This fallback can still steal the tap that the point-based resolver intentionally rejected. On mobile `touchend.target` stays as the element where the touch started, so if a touch starts on a text input, drifts less than `INPUT_TAP_MOVE_THRESHOLD`, and ends over a nearby button, `resolveKeyboardTouchTargetFromPoint()` returns `null` for the interactive button, but this fallback reselects the original input. The code then calls `preventDefault()`, suppresses the native button click, focuses the input, and dispatches the replacement click to the input instead. Consider making the fallback conditional on the lift point not being an interactive/label target, or returning an explicit blocked result from the point resolver.

 By default, the drawer can skip snap points when swiping quickly. Specify the `snapToSequentialPoints` prop to disable velocity-based skipping so the snap target is determined by drag distance (you can still drag past multiple points).
 
+### Virtual keyboard aware
+
+Wrap a bottom sheet in `<Drawer.VirtualKeyboardProvider>` to make it react to software keyboards when it contains form controls.
+
+Place header and footer content outside a plain scrollable body so the popup frame stays stable. When the keyboard opens, the provider scrolls the body to keep the focused field visible.
+
+If a footer contains its own input, reserve a footer slot below the scroll area and lift the pinned footer with `--drawer-keyboard-inset`. In the demo, the focused footer switches to `position: fixed` — positioned against the popup, since its `transform` contains fixed descendants — and adds the inset to its bottom padding.
body: 🟡 The docs should show the fallback form for this CSS variable. The provider removes `--drawer-keyboard-inset` on cleanup and only sets it during alignment/reset, so CSS like `calc(1rem + var(--drawer-keyboard-inset))` becomes invalid before the first keyboard alignment or after cleanup. The demos already use `var(--drawer-keyboard-inset, 0px)`; this prose/API wording should teach that form too.
